name: PICO-8 for PS5
description: Unofficial loader that runs your own copy of the PICO-8 Linux build as a native PS5 app.
author: RafaelNGP
release_notes:
PICO-8 for PS5 runs the official PICO-8 for Linux (bring your own license) as a native app with its own Home icon on a jailbroken PS5.

Unofficial project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Lexaloffle. PICO-8 itself is not included: you need your own PICO-8 Linux 64-bit copy (tested with 0.2.7).

Installation
- Extract PPSA99808.zip and copy the PPSA99808 folder, as a whole, to /data/homebrew/ on the PS5.
- From your PICO-8 Linux zip, copy pico8_dyn and pico8.dat into PPSA99808/pico8/.
- Within ~15 s, ShadowMountPlus adds the PICO-8 icon to the Home screen.

Requirements: kstuff, ShadowMountPlus, and elfldr listening on 127.0.0.1:9021 (used to get access to /data). Full instructions are in PPSA99808/README.txt.

Updating from v0.1.x: close the app and copy the new PPSA99808 folder over the old one. Your pico8/ files and your saves are kept. If the Home screen keeps the old icon, delete the PICO-8 icon from the Home screen (only the icon, not the folder) and ShadowMountPlus adds it again within ~15 s.

Changes since v0.1.1
- PICO-8 logo as the app icon, replacing the generic "P8" icon.
- New package layout: the asset is now always called PPSA99808.zip, with the PPSA99808 folder at its root (the format used by the PS5 homebrew catalog). README.txt, LICENSE and licenses/ are now inside that folder. Direct link to the latest version: https://github.com/RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5/releases/latest/download/PPSA99808.zip
- contentVersion 01.001.002, so consoles and stores can detect updates.

Known limitations
- USB keyboards and the on-screen keyboard don't work.
- Tested on a single PS5. Other firmware versions may need adjustments.

Reporting a problem: please attach /data/pico8/loader.log and say which firmware you're on.

The app icon is the PICO-8 logo, (c) Lexaloffle Games; it is not covered by the GPL. The SHA-256 of the zip is in PPSA99808.zip.sha256.
